description: Draws pictures for a motion film on fal and links them to the video, so the film shows the thing itself (a person, a building, a product, an animal, a scene) and never a placeholder. kind "cutout": one subject on a transparent background, trimmed to it, to move like a paper puppet; kind "backdrop": a whole scene filling the frame (shape tall for a vertical film). Every picture of a film shares one style (the same words each call, with the film's palette colours named in it). Key pictures first: draw the main character and one backdrop alone, look at them, and only then the rest, each with like: the key pictures, so a picture keeps the style far better than words do. follow: names of earlier pictures whose character or design this one keeps (a second pose of the same person). from: names of pictures already on the video (uploaded, fetched or drawn) to draw from, e.g. a photo of their product redrawn in the film's style. like: names of pictures whose drawing style only it matches (line, palette, shading, light), never what they show; a backdrop takes the key character in like, never in follow, or the character turns up in it. model: nano-banana (fast and the cheapest, fine for simple cut-outs); nano-banana-2 (the default: good drawings, keeps a character the same across poses); nano-banana-pro (the most detailed and the best at lettering, about twice the price); prices in the guide. Lettering inside a picture is allowed when they want it (a sign, a label); the models spell well but not perfectly, so check the sheet. Each picture is in useFilm().assets under its name: show it with remotion's (a.width / a.height give its shape); the tool returns a sheet of them to look at. Up to 12 a call, 40 a video. Uses their credits; leave pictures out to list the video's pictures.

model.description: The drawing model; nano-banana-2 unless they want cheaper or finer

pictures.description: Up to 12 pictures a call; leave out to list the video's pictures

follow.description: Names of pictures it keeps the same character or design as; empty for none

from.description: Names of pictures on the video to draw from (a photo, a logo); empty for none

like.description: Names of the film's key pictures whose drawing style it matches, never their subject; empty for a key picture itself

name.description: Unique within the video, e.g. pharaoh, pharaoh-pointing, giza-backdrop

prompt.description: What it shows, drawn from the voiceover line said while it is on screen: the subject, the pose and expression that line needs, details, the camera angle, the empty area its words will sit on, and the film's one light direction; for a backdrop the whole scene; any lettering it should carry, spelled out

shape.description: For a backdrop: the film's shape (tall for vertical); a cutout is trimmed to its subject whatever this says

style.description: The art style in words, the same for every picture of this film (line, colour, shading, era-accurate costume); required when drawing

name: pictures
title: Draw pictures for the film
